newsitem.title: CANADA: Salomon rates PanCanadian as a hold.
newsitem.headline: Salomon rates PanCanadian as a hold.

text.p: New York-based Salomon Brothers analyst Zev Grossman said on Friday he started coverage of PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd with a hold rating.
Grossman said his 12-month target price for Calgary-based PanCanadian was C$32 a share, offering about 18 percent growth in the stock.
The hold rating was based on the company's limited opportunities in Canada to re-invest its C$1 billion in annual cash flow, he said.
The company's ownership structure -- Canadian Pacific Ltd controls 87 percent of PanCanadian's stock -- also presented limitations, he said.
Grossman said although PanCanadian was Canada's second-largest oil and gas company, it was ranked only 16th in terms of public float, which limited liquidity.
Further, he said the stock was fairly valued, trading at 115 percent of net asset value, which was in line with its peers.
A major international acquisition was a likely solution to PanCanadian's limited Canadian opportunities and a deal could drive the stock up "significantly," Grossman said.
PanCanadian has made it known for several months now that it is in the market for an international deal valued at over C$1 billion.
"However, a big international acquisition, while frequently talked about, could be a long way off," said Grossman.
"In our view, a better way to play the upside is to own shares of the partner Canadian Pacific, which we rate as a buy." ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
